H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: H-OS-L1 (Pebble, n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong) is the most robust data point in HEALING and the entire dataset. Distribution clusters strongly at 7–9 (41/95) with 17 scores at 9. Qualitative data (n=29) shows settle time at 5–10 minutes, change ratings dominated by 'Noticeable improvement' (12/29), and music strongly positive (10 liked, 9 loved). YouTube reach is the highest in the dataset at 30 views, though retention data is unavailable. AutoGluon predicts 6.86 for overstimulation zone, slightly below observed, indicating this protocol may outperform model expectations. This is both the most well-founded and most discovered protocol.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: Pebble is the most thoroughly tested protocol in the library. Most people with over-stimulation felt noticeable improvement within 5–10 minutes, and the music was widely loved. It's the standout performer.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: H-OS-L2 (Rainfall, n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong) shows slightly lower mean than L1 but strong confidence. Distribution is left-skewed toward 7–8. Qualitative data (n=21) shows settle time at 10 minutes (10/21) and change ratings dominated by 'Noticeable improvement' (10). Music opinions split (10 liked, 6 neutral). YouTube views (5) are minimal. AutoGluon prediction (6.86) aligns closely with observed. The pattern suggests comparable efficacy to L1 but slightly less dramatic effect.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Rainfall works well for over-stimulation, similar to Pebble but with slightly less dramatic effects. The music got split reviews. It's solid but less striking.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: H-OS-L3 (Glacier, n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) rebounds above L2 with the tightest std in the over-stimulation group (1.68). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (21/47). Qualitative data (n=23) shows settle time split between 5 and 10 minutes, with notable activity at 'trying to sleep' (8/23) — a crossover signal with sleep protocols. Music: 11 liked, 5 neutral. AutoGluon predicts 6.86, slightly below observed. This protocol appears effective and consistent with a potential secondary use case for sleep onset.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Glacier is consistent and effective for over-stimulation, and notably, several people used it when trying to fall asleep. It works well and may have a secondary benefit for sleep onset.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: H-AX-L1 (Meadow, n=67, mean=7.22, std=1.93, confidence=strong) leads the Anxiety & Stress family with a right-skewed distribution peaking at scores 7 and 10. The wide standard deviation indicates meaningful listener variability, possibly driven by clinician representation in qualitative data (6 of 23 respondents) who may rate on a different implicit scale than self-listeners. Qualitative context shows modal settle time at 'About 10 minutes' (9/23) with change ratings dominated by 'Moderate Improvement' (10/23) and music opinions strongly positive (13 liked, 6 loved). YouTube reach remains minimal at 7 views with no retention data, consistent with early adoption phase. AutoGluon predicts 7.838 for the anxiety zone, modestly above observed mean, suggesting untapped potential or model optimism. The adviser source (5/67) indicates some guided discovery but predominantly organic uptake.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Most listeners with anxiety or stress found Meadow noticeably helpful within about 10 minutes. The music was well-liked, and while experiences varied, the overall response was clearly positive. This is the most tested anxiety protocol so far.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: H-AX-L2 (Cottage, n=48, mean=6.94, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful) shows a tighter distribution than L1, concentrated in the 7–8 range with 15 of 48 responses clustered there. Qualitative data (n=20) splits between self-listeners (12) and clinicians (6) with notably fast modal settle time at 'About 5 minutes' (9/20), aligning with the lower variance in outcome scores. Change ratings distribute across 'Noticeable' (6), 'Moderate' (6), and 'Slight' (5) improvement with no 'Significant' reports, suggesting this protocol works more gradually than L1. Music opinions show more neutral responses (5/20) compared to L1. YouTube views (6) are negligible. The 0.28-point drop from L1 warrants monitoring as n grows — it may reflect a genuine L2 inflection in the DESCENT curve or sample composition differences.
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: Cottage helps with anxiety but works more gradually — most people settled in about 5 minutes. The music got mixed reviews, some loved it, others found it just okay. It's reliable but less dramatic than Meadow.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: H-AX-L3 (Valley, n=36, mean=7.08, std=1.89, confidence=meaningful) sits between L1 and L2 in mean score with an unusual bimodal pattern: peaks at scores 7–8 and a secondary cluster at score 10 (5 responses). Qualitative data (n=20) shows 'About 10 minutes' as the dominant settle time — longer than L2's 5-minute mode — and 'Noticeable improvement' as the modal change rating (8/20). Five respondents reported 'No effect' and 5 rated music 'Neutral', signaling potential polarization. YouTube views (4) are the lowest in the H-AX family. This protocol may be a deeper DESCENT requiring more listener commitment, with the longer settle time and moderate outcomes warranting attention.
H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: Valley takes a bit longer to work (around 10 minutes) and some people didn't feel much effect. The music got neutral reviews. It may be a deeper, slower protocol that needs more patience.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor
H-CR-L1.sphere: H-CR-L1 (Anchor, n=43, mean=6.35, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) shows the expected lower mean for a crisis protocol serving listeners in acute distress baselines. The distribution has notable concentration at score 8 (12/43), suggesting a responsive subpopulation. Qualitative data (n=24) reveals the highest 'Significant improvement' rating in the dataset (8/24), indicating this protocol may be highly effective for a specific subgroup despite moderate aggregate. Music opinions are positive (11 liked, 5 loved) with balanced rhythm feedback (11 balanced, 6 very settling). Settle time splits between 5 and 10 minutes. AutoGluon predicts 7.96 for the crisis zone — a substantial 1.61-point gap above observed — flagging a discrepancy worth investigating for acute-distress delivery.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: Anchor helps people in acute distress, with many reporting significant improvement within 5–10 minutes. The music is calming and well-liked. Results vary — it seems to work very well for some but less for others.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor
H-CR-L2.sphere: H-CR-L2 (Harbor, n=33, mean=6.52, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) shows slightly higher mean than L1 with comparable spread. Distribution peaks at 7–8 (15/33). Qualitative data (n=16) shows more mixed music feedback (6 neutral, 5 loved) — the only crisis protocol with neutral-as-dominant music opinion. Change ratings cluster at 'Moderate' (6) and 'Noticeable' (5) improvement. Settle time spreads across 5–10 minutes. AutoGluon predicts 7.96, again far exceeding observed. The pattern suggests this protocol works but may feel different sonically than L1, with the model-observation gap reinforcing the need to examine crisis protocol design.
H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: Harbor also helps in crisis situations but the music got more mixed reactions — some found it neutral. It works similarly to Anchor but feels different sonically.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon
H-CR-L3.sphere: H-CR-L3 (Horizon, n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91, confidence=meaningful) matches L2's mean but with notably higher variance (std=1.91 vs 1.70) and a slightly bimodal distribution: 6 responses at score 10 but 5 at score 4. Qualitative data (n=19) shows the fastest settle time of any crisis protocol: 7/19 report 'Immediately/within first minute or two' — a striking signal of rapid entrainment for some listeners. Music opinions split between liked (7) and not liked (4). This protocol may be highly effective for certain listeners but polarizing for others, with the highest variance in the crisis family.
H-CR-L3.sphere_plain: Horizon works fastest for some people in crisis — several felt better almost immediately. But it's polarizing: some loved it, others really didn't. It may suit certain listeners perfectly and miss others entirely.

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern
H-SL-L1.sphere: H-SL-L1 (Lantern, n=54, mean=7.19, std=1.86, confidence=strong) is the top performer in HEALING sleep category. Distribution clusters at 8–10 (25/54) with 11 scores at 9 and 5 at 10. Qualitative data (n=15) shows fast settle (5 at 5 min, 3 immediate), music: 10 liked, 3 loved. Change ratings are positive. AutoGluon predicts 7.54 for sleep zone, modestly above observed. YouTube views (8) remain low — potential for discovery. Embedding drift for this protocol is notable (0.530), flagging analytical instability across runs.
H-SL-L1.sphere_plain: Lantern is the top sleep protocol — most people settled quickly (within 5 minutes) and really liked the music. It's a strong performer that more people should discover.

H-SL-L2.name: Hammock
H-SL-L2.sphere: H-SL-L2 (Hammock, n=45, mean=7.09, std=1.55, confidence=meaningful) has the tightest std in the entire HEALING series (1.55). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (23/45). Notably, qualitative data (n=15) shows listener_type skew toward 'client/patient' (6) and 'someone I support' (5) rather than 'myself' (4) — it may be used in clinical settings. Music opinions are neutral-dominant (6/15) — the only HEALING protocol with this pattern. This deserves investigation: the most statistically consistent protocol may be underperforming musically. AutoGluon predicts 7.54 vs observed 7.09. YouTube views (5) are negligible.
H-SL-L2.sphere_plain: Hammock is statistically the most consistent sleep protocol, but the music got neutral reviews, and it's mostly being used by caregivers or clinicians rather than people listening for themselves. That's worth looking into.

H-SL-L3.name: Midnight
H-SL-L3.sphere: H-SL-L3 (Midnight, n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) is consistent with L1 and L2, with slight std reduction. Distribution centers at 6–9. Qualitative data (n=22) shows settle at 5–10 minutes, music split (8 liked, 6 neutral). AutoGluon predicts 7.54 again above observed, indicating persistent model overestimation for sleep zone. YouTube views (3) are negligible. This protocol performs as expected in the sleep category.
H-SL-L3.sphere_plain: Midnight performs reliably for sleep, with quick settling and generally positive feedback. It does what it's designed to do.

T-FC-L1.name: Compass
T-FC-L1.sphere: T-FC-L1 (Compass, n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful) is the lowest-scoring THRIVING protocol and the lowest in Focus & Clarity. Distribution peaks at 7 (12/41). Qualitative (n=23) shows 'Slightly busy' rhythm opinion as dominant complaint (9/23) — the highest rhythm complaint count in the dataset. Settle at 5–10 min. AutoGluon predicts 7.728 for focus zone — a 1.27-point gap suggesting major unmet promise. YouTube views (6) negligible. This rhythm pacing issue is a primary development signal.
T-FC-L1.sphere_plain: Compass is the lowest-scoring focus protocol. Many listeners found the rhythm 'slightly busy' — it may be too rhythmically complex for focus work. This needs adjustment.

T-FC-L2.name: Waypoint
T-FC-L2.sphere: T-FC-L2 (Waypoint, n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful) shows a notable jump from L1. Distribution clusters at 8–9 (12/32). Qualitative (n=17) shows settle at 10 min (9/17) — longer settling but higher outcomes. Music neutral (6), but 5 loved it. Change ratings strong (5 moderate, 5 significant). AutoGluon predicts 7.728, close to observed. This protocol works but may require patience. YouTube views (4) minimal.
T-FC-L2.sphere_plain: Waypoint works well for focus but takes patience — most people settled around 10 minutes. The music is neutral but the results are strong.

T-FC-L3.name: Summit
T-FC-L3.sphere: T-FC-L3 (Summit, n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful) is the highest mean in the dataset with a striking distribution: 10 responses at score 10 — the highest concentration of perfect scores. Qualitative (n=29) shows 15/29 settle at 10 minutes, music: liked (12), loved (8), rhythm: balanced (15). AutoGluon predicts 7.728, aligning almost exactly with observed — excellent model alignment. YouTube reach (17 views) is the highest in THRIVING. This is a top performer with cross-bucket routing signals to mind clarity and motivation zones.
T-FC-L3.sphere_plain: Summit is the highest-scoring protocol in the entire library. People loved the music, found the rhythm balanced, and reported significant improvement. It's a standout for focus and clarity.

T-CF-L1.name: Ember
T-CF-L1.sphere: T-CF-L1 (Ember, n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, confidence=meaningful) is a Creative Flow HOLD protocol below the THRIVING series mean. Distribution is fairly uniform across 5–9. Qualitative data (n=21) shows polarization: 8/21 'Slight improvement' vs 6/21 'Significant improvement' — reflecting the std and indicating this protocol works dramatically for some but not others. Settle time fastest at immediate + 10 min (6 each). Music: 9 liked, 6 loved. AutoGluon cross-routes to mind clarity zone (predicted 7.538), suggesting functional convergence. YouTube views (2) negligible.
T-CF-L1.sphere_plain: Ember helps some people enter creative flow dramatically, while others only notice slight change. The music is liked, but the experience is polarized — it's not consistent across listeners.

T-CF-L2.name: Current
T-CF-L2.sphere: T-CF-L2 (Current, n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful) has the tightest std in THRIVING (1.41). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (14/24). Qualitative (n=15) shows 'Significant improvement' dominant (5/15), music: loved (6), liked (6). This is the most consistent THRIVING protocol with high satisfaction among responders. Settle time around 5–10 minutes. YouTube views (2) minimal. AutoGluon does not flag this protocol specifically.
T-CF-L2.sphere_plain: Current is the most consistent creative flow protocol — people who respond to it respond well. The music is loved. It works reliably for those it works for.

T-CF-L3.name: Aurora
T-CF-L3.sphere: T-CF-L3 (Aurora, n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, confidence=developing) achieves the highest mean in THRIVING with the tightest std (1.32). Distribution skewed right. Qualitative data (n=25, exceeding 1-second n) shows settle at 10 and 5 minutes (7 each), music: liked (9), neutral (7). The qualitative n exceeding outcome n suggests possible lag in outcome data collection. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mind clarity zone with cross-bucket routing, suggesting functional convergence. This protocol shows strong promise despite developing confidence tier.
T-CF-L3.sphere_plain: Aurora shows the strongest results for creative flow so far, with high scores and consistent feedback. It's promising but still early days with fewer total listeners.

T-MB-L1.name: Stone
T-MB-L1.sphere: T-MB-L1 (Stone, n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, confidence=meaningful) shows tight std and right-skewed distribution. Qualitative (n=23) shows settle at 20 minutes (9/23) — longest in category — suggesting slower entrainment for maintenance protocols. Music: 6 neutral, 6 liked. AutoGluon predicts 7.693 for maintenance zone, exceeding observed, suggesting underperformance. YouTube views (3) negligible.
T-MB-L1.sphere_plain: Stone works for maintenance and balance but takes time — many people needed 20 minutes to settle. The music got neutral reviews. It's effective but slow.

T-MB-L2.name: Axis
T-MB-L2.sphere: T-MB-L2 (Axis, n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, confidence=meaningful) has the highest variance in THRIVING (std=2.03). Distribution shows spread with some reporting no effect and others rating highly. Qualitative (n=16) shows 7 respondents noting 'Slightly busy' rhythm — suggesting overstimulation risk in a maintenance protocol. Settle time delayed for some. AutoGluon predicts 7.693, well above observed, indicating a large model-actual gap. YouTube views (4) minimal. This variability and rhythm signal warrant investigation.
T-MB-L2.sphere_plain: Axis is hit or miss — some people report no effect, others rate it highly. Several found the rhythm too busy for a calming protocol. It's inconsistent and may need rhythm adjustment.

T-MB-L3.name: Orbit
T-MB-L3.sphere: T-MB-L3 (Orbit, n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, confidence=developing) achieves one of the highest positive-response rates in THRIVING (71% positive). Qualitative (n=19) shows settle rapid for some (8/19) though 4 reported 'Did not settle'. Music opinion mixed. AutoGluon predicts 7.693, again above observed. YouTube views (3) low. Small n limits confidence but positive rate is notable.
T-MB-L3.sphere_plain: Orbit has a high rate of positive responses for maintenance, though some didn't settle at all. Music reviews are mixed. Promising but early data.

X-ME-L1.name: Breeze
X-ME-L1.sphere: X-ME-L1 (Breeze, n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful) sits below TRANSFORMING average with moderate variance. Settling times long (20 minutes reported 6/22 qualitative). Music feedback polarized. AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone — significantly above observed — suggesting the protocol may be effective for very low-affect states not yet captured in outcome model. Cross-bucket routing confirms low zone prediction. YouTube views (8) minimal.
X-ME-L1.sphere_plain: Breeze hasn't hit its stride for mood and energy yet. Settling takes a long time (20 minutes for several people) and music feedback is split. The model thinks it should work for very low states — but we're not seeing it.

X-ME-L2.name: Sunrise
X-ME-L2.sphere: X-ME-L2 (Sunrise, n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful) shows better performance than L1 with faster settling and more positive music feedback. Qualitative (n=15) shows settle at 10 minutes (7/15) and 5 minutes (4/15), with music 'Liked' (7) and 'Loved' (5). AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone vs observed 6.76 — a persistent gap. YouTube views (8) minimal. This protocol appears more accessible than L1 but still underperforms model expectations.
X-ME-L2.sphere_plain: Sunrise is better than Breeze — faster settling, better music feedback — but still well below model predictions. It's more accessible but not there yet.

X-ME-L3.name: Updraft
X-ME-L3.sphere: X-ME-L3 (Updraft, n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing) is the lowest-scoring Mood & Energy protocol. Qualitative (n=18) shows settle at 5 minutes (8/18), music 'Liked' (5), 'Loved' (4). Change ratings: 'Noticeable' (7), 'Moderate' (5), 'Significant' (4). AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone — a massive gap. YouTube views (6) minimal. Small n and developing confidence limit interpretation but the model-observation divergence is consistent across the X-ME family.
X-ME-L3.sphere_plain: Updraft is the lowest mood/energy protocol. Quick settling for some, decent music, but the model expects far more. Early data, big gap.

X-MD-L1.name: Footpath
X-MD-L1.sphere: X-MD-L1 (Footpath, n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful) is one of the weakest TRANSFORMING protocols with mean below 6.4 and only 45% positive — the lowest positive rate in the library. Most report slight or moderate improvement with delayed settling (20 minutes for 5/17 qualitative). AutoGluon predicts 7.876 — the highest predicted score among all protocols — but this protocol underperforms drastically with a 1.52-point gap. Cross-bucket routing confirms intended motivation zone. YouTube views (5) minimal. This is a major model-observation misalignment.
X-MD-L1.sphere_plain: Footpath is the weakest motivation protocol. Most people report only slight improvement and it takes a long time to settle. The model expects much more — there's a real disconnect.

X-MD-L2.name: Trail
X-MD-L2.sphere: X-MD-L2 (Trail, n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing) shows consistently low performance with 43% positive. Some report no effect; settling delayed. AutoGluon predicts 7.876, far above observed, indicating major misalignment. YouTube views (7) minimal. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity — possibly indicating functional overlap between motivation and clarity protocols.
X-MD-L2.sphere_plain: Trail consistently underperforms for motivation. Low engagement, delayed settling. The model predicts it should work much better — something's misaligned.

X-MD-L3.name: Switchback
X-MD-L3.sphere: X-MD-L3 (Switchback, n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing) is a paradoxical result: high mean despite high variance and low n. Qualitative (n=17) reports 'moderate improvement' for some, 'no effect' for others. Settle rapid for 9/13. AutoGluon predicts 7.876, still above observed. YouTube views (7) low. Embedding drift is notable (0.507). This protocol may resonate with a specific subpopulation but the high variance and small n prevent firm conclusions.
X-MD-L3.sphere_plain: Switchback is puzzling — high average score but very mixed individual results and a small sample. It works dramatically for some, not at all for others. Hard to read with this little data.

X-MC-L1.name: Cavern
X-MC-L1.sphere: X-MC-L1 (Cavern, n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful) sits below average for TRANSFORMING. Distribution shows clustering at 6–7. Qualitative (n=25) includes some citing 'it actually made things worse' (2/25) — a red flag. Settling delayed for 16/24. Music opinion overwhelmingly positive. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mind clarity zone, significantly higher than observed, suggesting misalignment. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity — consistent with protocol design but data confirms functional relevance with delivery gaps.
X-MC-L1.sphere_plain: Cavern helps some people with mind clarity but others report delayed settling or even feeling worse. The music is liked but the protocol may not be landing correctly for everyone.

X-MC-L2.name: Starlight
X-MC-L2.sphere: X-MC-L2 (Starlight, n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, confidence=developing) shows stable but underwhelming performance. Qualitative (n=20) includes moderate improvement from 6 but some 'no effect'. AutoGluon predicts 7.538, significantly higher than observed, indicating a large real-expected gap. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity. YouTube views (12) are the highest in TRANSFORMING but still minimal.
X-MC-L2.sphere_plain: Starlight is stable but underwhelming for mind clarity. Some report moderate improvement, others no effect. It's not hitting its mark consistently yet.

X-MC-L3.name: Cosmos
X-MC-L3.sphere: X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing) records the lowest mean in the entire library with the widest variance and a bimodal distribution. Two respondents reported significant improvement, five rated 7–8, but five rated 5 or lower. Qualitative (n=17) shows some improvement but also 'no effect' and one 'worse'. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 — an extreme 1.84-point gap indicating severe underperformance. YouTube views (8) very low. This protocol warrants prototype revision of frequency arc or duration.
X-MC-L3.sphere_plain: Cosmos is the lowest-scoring protocol in the library. Results are all over the place — some helped, some not, one person felt worse. It needs a redesign.

sphere_commentary.overview:
Aggregate data across 1,000 outcome responses reveals broadly positive signals across all three series, with TRANSFORMING trailing modestly as expected given its ascending-arc design for low-affect states.
• HEALING and THRIVING share nearly identical overall means (6.98 vs 6.96) despite serving different nervous system states
• TRANSFORMING shows the widest variance (std=1.87), consistent with the structural challenge of lifting listeners from low-affect baselines
• HEALING dominates in data volume (574 responses) and confidence-tier density, with 4 of 12 protocols at strong confidence
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series-level means aggregate different protocol types, complicating direct comparison, but design intent aligns with observed patterns.
• HEALING: DESCENT protocols cluster tightly around 7.0 across anxiety, crisis, over-stimulation, and sleep entry points with reliable entrainment
• THRIVING: HOLD protocols show bimodal efficacy — Focus & Clarity peaks at 7.63 (T-FC-L3) while Creative Flow and Maintenance show wider spread
• TRANSFORMING: ASCENT protocols (Mood & Energy, Motivation & Drive) consistently score below 7.0, reinforcing the design challenge of ascending from low-affect states
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several distribution shapes and qualitative signals warrant investigation beyond point estimates.
• T-FC-L3 (Summit, n=35) shows heavy right tail with 10 scores of 10 while T-FC-L1 (Compass, n=41) sits at 6.46 — a 1.17 delta within the same entry zone
• X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10) records the lowest mean (5.70) and highest std (2.45) in the library, suggesting possible sub-group effect or small-sample instability
• X-MD-L3 (Switchback, n=13) stands as an outlier among Motivation protocols (L1: 6.36, L2: 6.21) at mean 7.15 with std 2.38
• H-CR protocols (combined n=103) show compressed distributions with few scores above 8 despite qualitative reports of rapid settling, suggesting DESCENT curve depth may be insufficient for acute distress
• H-SL-L2 (Hammock, n=45) qualitative data shows listener mix dominated by clients and caregivers (11 of 15), not self-listeners, potentially influencing change ratings
• AutoGluon vs observed gaps: H-CR protocols predicted ~7.9 vs observed ~6.4-6.5; X-MD-L1 predicted 7.88 vs observed 6.36; X-MC-L3 predicted 7.54 vs observed 5.70
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Convergent signals across multiple analyzers identify four priority development targets.
• T-FC-L1 (Compass, n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82) — 9 of 23 contextual respondents report 'Slightly busy' rhythm; investigate whether HOLD-phase rhythm complexity disrupts focus entrainment
• H-CR family (L1/L2/L3, combined n=103) — all three show structurally lower means and compressed upper tails; investigate whether DESCENT curve depth or duration is sufficient for acute distress baselines
• X-MD-L1 (Footpath, n=22, mean=6.36, pct_pos=45%) — only protocol below 50% positive rating; AutoGluon predicts 7.88 (largest gap in library); explore ASCENT onset timing mismatch for motivation protocols
• X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45) — prototype revised frequency arc or shorter duration and re-test; developing confidence with extreme model-observation gap
• H-OS-L1 (Pebble, n=95, mean=7.15) — strongest HEALING protocol with highest YouTube reach (30 views); prioritize scaling across additional volumes
• T-MB-L2 (Axis, n=22, std=2.03) — highest THRIVING variance with 7 respondents noting 'Slightly busy' rhythm; investigate groove mismatch for maintenance protocols
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift data reveals widespread analytical instability across all tracked protocols.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: All 30 protocols with comparative data show notable drift (cosine similarity 0.507–0.821), with lowest stability in X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), X-ME-L2 (0.532)
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Insufficient embeddings for reliable clustering — only one run's embeddings available
• Confidence note: Drift signals are based on only two data points per protocol (earliest vs most recent run) and may reflect genuine data evolution rather than analytical inconsistency; more runs needed to distinguish signal from noise

Music opinions show more neutral responses (5/20) compared to L1. YouTube views (6) are negligible. by_protocol.H-AX-L3: H-AX-L3 (Valley, n=36, mean=7.08, std=1.89, confidence=meaningful) sits between L1 and L2 in mean score with an unusual bimodal pattern: peaks at scores 7–8 and a secondary cluster at score 10 (5 responses). Qualitative data (n=20) shows 'About 10 minutes' as the dominant settle time — longer than L2's 5-minute mode — and 'Noticeable improvement' as the modal change rating (8/20). Five respondents reported 'No effect' and 5 rated music 'Neutral', signaling potential polarization. YouTube views (4) are the lowest in the H-AX family. This protocol may be a deeper DESCENT requiring more listener commitment, with the longer settle time and moderate outcomes warranting attention.
by_protocol.H-CR-L1: H-CR-L1 (Anchor, n=43, mean=6.35, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) shows the expected lower mean for a crisis protocol serving listeners in acute distress baselines. The distribution has notable concentration at score 8 (12/43), suggesting a responsive subpopulation. Qualitative data (n=24) reveals the highest 'Significant improvement' rating in the dataset (8/24), indicating this protocol may be highly effective for a specific subgroup despite moderate aggregate. Music opinions are positive (11 liked, 5 loved) with balanced rhythm feedback (11 balanced, 6 very settling). Settle time splits between 5 and 10 minutes. AutoGluon predicts 7.96 for the crisis zone — a substantial 1.61-point gap above observed — flagging a discrepancy worth investigating for acute-distress delivery.
by_protocol.H-CR-L2: H-CR-L2 (Harbor, n=33, mean=6.52, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) shows slightly higher mean than L1 with comparable spread. Distribution peaks at 7–8 (15/33). Qualitative data (n=16) shows more mixed music feedback (6 neutral, 5 loved) — the only crisis protocol with neutral-as-dominant music opinion. Change ratings cluster at 'Moderate' (6) and 'Noticeable' (5) improvement. Settle time spreads across 5–10 minutes. AutoGluon predicts 7.96, again far exceeding observed. The pattern suggests this protocol works but may feel different sonically than L1, with the model-observation gap reinforcing the need to examine crisis protocol design.
by_protocol.H-CR-L3: H-CR-L3 (Horizon, n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91, confidence=meaningful) matches L2's mean but with notably higher variance (std=1.91 vs 1.70) and a slightly bimodal distribution: 6 responses at score 10 but 5 at score 4. Qualitative data (n=19) shows the fastest settle time of any crisis protocol: 7/19 report 'Immediately/within first minute or two' — a striking signal of rapid entrainment for some listeners. Music opinions split between liked (7) and not liked (4). This protocol may be highly effective for certain listeners but polarizing for others, with the highest variance in the crisis family.
by_protocol.H-OS-L1: H-OS-L1 (Pebble, n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong) is the most robust data point in HEALING and the entire dataset. Distribution clusters strongly at 7–9 (41/95) with 17 scores at 9. Qualitative data (n=29) shows settle time at 5–10 minutes, change ratings dominated by 'Noticeable improvement' (12/29), and music strongly positive (10 liked, 9 loved). YouTube reach is the highest in the dataset at 30 views, though retention data is unavailable. AutoGluon predicts 6.86 for overstimulation zone, slightly below observed, indicating this protocol may outperform model expectations. This is both the most well-founded and most discovered protocol.
by_protocol.H-OS-L2: H-OS-L2 (Rainfall, n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong) shows slightly lower mean than L1 but strong confidence. Distribution is left-skewed toward 7–8. Qualitative data (n=21) shows settle time at 10 minutes (10/21) and change ratings dominated by 'Noticeable improvement' (10). Music opinions split (10 liked, 6 neutral). YouTube views (5) are minimal. AutoGluon prediction (6.86) aligns closely with observed. The pattern suggests comparable efficacy to L1 but slightly less dramatic effect.
by_protocol.H-OS-L3: H-OS-L3 (Glacier, n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) rebounds above L2 with the tightest std in the over-stimulation group (1.68). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (21/47). Qualitative data (n=23) shows settle time split between 5 and 10 minutes, with notable activity at 'trying to sleep' (8/23) — a crossover signal with sleep protocols. Music: 11 liked, 5 neutral. AutoGluon predicts 6.86, slightly below observed. This protocol appears effective and consistent with a potential secondary use case for sleep onset.
by_protocol.H-SL-L1: H-SL-L1 (Lantern, n=54, mean=7.19, std=1.86, confidence=strong) is the top performer in HEALING sleep category. Distribution clusters at 8–10 (25/54) with 11 scores at 9 and 5 at 10. Qualitative data (n=15) shows fast settle (5 at 5 min, 3 immediate), music: 10 liked, 3 loved. Change ratings are positive. AutoGluon predicts 7.54 for sleep zone, modestly above observed. YouTube views (8) remain low — potential for discovery. Embedding drift for this protocol is notable (0.530), flagging analytical instability across runs.
by_protocol.H-SL-L2: H-SL-L2 (Hammock, n=45, mean=7.09, std=1.55, confidence=meaningful) has the tightest std in the entire HEALING series (1.55). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (23/45). Notably, qualitative data (n=15) shows listener_type skew toward 'client/patient' (6) and 'someone I support' (5) rather than 'myself' (4) — it may be used in clinical settings. Music opinions are neutral-dominant (6/15) — the only HEALING protocol with this pattern. This deserves investigation: the most statistically consistent protocol may be underperforming musically. AutoGluon predicts 7.54 vs observed 7.09. YouTube views (5) are negligible.
by_protocol.H-SL-L3: H-SL-L3 (Midnight, n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) is consistent with L1 and L2, with slight std reduction. Distribution centers at 6–9. Qualitative data (n=22) shows settle at 5–10 minutes, music split (8 liked, 6 neutral). AutoGluon predicts 7.54 again above observed, indicating persistent model overestimation for sleep zone. YouTube views (3) are negligible. This protocol performs as expected in the sleep category.
by_protocol.T-CF-L1: T-CF-L1 (Ember, n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, confidence=meaningful) is a Creative Flow HOLD protocol below the THRIVING series mean. Distribution is fairly uniform across 5–9. Qualitative data (n=21) shows polarization: 8/21 'Slight improvement' vs 6/21 'Significant improvement' — reflecting the std and indicating this protocol works dramatically for some but not others. Settle time fastest at immediate + 10 min (6 each). Music: 9 liked, 6 loved. AutoGluon cross-routes to mind clarity zone (predicted 7.538), suggesting functional convergence. YouTube views (2) negligible.
by_protocol.T-CF-L2: T-CF-L2 (Current, n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful) has the tightest std in THRIVING (1.41). Distribution clusters at 7–8 (14/24). Qualitative (n=15) shows 'Significant improvement' dominant (5/15), music: loved (6), liked (6). This is the most consistent THRIVING protocol with high satisfaction among responders. Settle time around 5–10 minutes. YouTube views (2) minimal. AutoGluon does not flag this protocol specifically.
by_protocol.T-CF-L3: T-CF-L3 (Aurora, n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, confidence=developing) achieves the highest mean in THRIVING with the tightest std (1.32). Distribution skewed right. Qualitative data (n=25, exceeding 1-second n) shows settle at 10 and 5 minutes (7 each), music: liked (9), neutral (7). The qualitative n exceeding outcome n suggests possible lag in outcome data collection. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mind clarity zone with cross-bucket routing, suggesting functional convergence. This protocol shows strong promise despite developing confidence tier.
by_protocol.T-FC-L1: T-FC-L1 (Compass, n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful) is the lowest-scoring THRIVING protocol and the lowest in Focus & Clarity. Distribution peaks at 7 (12/41). Qualitative (n=23) shows 'Slightly busy' rhythm opinion as dominant complaint (9/23) — the highest rhythm complaint count in the dataset. Settle at 5–10 min. AutoGluon predicts 7.728 for focus zone — a 1.27-point gap suggesting major unmet promise. YouTube views (6) negligible. This rhythm pacing issue is a primary development signal.
by_protocol.T-FC-L2: T-FC-L2 (Waypoint, n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful) shows a notable jump from L1. Distribution clusters at 8–9 (12/32). Qualitative (n=17) shows settle at 10 min (9/17) — longer settling but higher outcomes. Music neutral (6), but 5 loved it. Change ratings strong (5 moderate, 5 significant). AutoGluon predicts 7.728, close to observed. This protocol works but may require patience. YouTube views (4) minimal.
by_protocol.T-FC-L3: T-FC-L3 (Summit, n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful) is the highest mean in the dataset with a striking distribution: 10 responses at score 10 — the highest concentration of perfect scores. Qualitative (n=29) shows 15/29 settle at 10 minutes, music: liked (12), loved (8), rhythm: balanced (15). AutoGluon predicts 7.728, aligning almost exactly with observed — excellent model alignment. YouTube reach (17 views) is the highest in THRIVING. This is a top performer with cross-bucket routing signals to mind clarity and motivation zones.
by_protocol.T-MB-L1: T-MB-L1 (Stone, n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, confidence=meaningful) shows tight std and right-skewed distribution. Qualitative (n=23) shows settle at 20 minutes (9/23) — longest in category — suggesting slower entrainment for maintenance protocols. Music: 6 neutral, 6 liked. AutoGluon predicts 7.693 for maintenance zone, exceeding observed, suggesting underperformance. YouTube views (3) negligible.
by_protocol.T-MB-L2: T-MB-L2 (Axis, n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, confidence=meaningful) has the highest variance in THRIVING (std=2.03). Distribution shows spread with some reporting no effect and others rating highly. Qualitative (n=16) shows 7 respondents noting 'Slightly busy' rhythm — suggesting overstimulation risk in a maintenance protocol. Settle time delayed for some. AutoGluon predicts 7.693, well above observed, indicating a large model-actual gap. YouTube views (4) minimal. This variability and rhythm signal warrant investigation.
by_protocol.T-MB-L3: T-MB-L3 (Orbit, n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, confidence=developing) achieves one of the highest positive-response rates in THRIVING (71% positive). Qualitative (n=19) shows settle rapid for some (8/19) though 4 reported 'Did not settle'. Music opinion mixed. AutoGluon predicts 7.693, again above observed. YouTube views (3) low. Small n limits confidence but positive rate is notable.
by_protocol.X-MC-L1: X-MC-L1 (Cavern, n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful) sits below average for TRANSFORMING. Distribution shows clustering at 6–7. Qualitative (n=25) includes some citing 'it actually made things worse' (2/25) — a red flag. Settling delayed for 16/24. Music opinion overwhelmingly positive. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mind clarity zone, significantly higher than observed, suggesting misalignment. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity — consistent with protocol design but data confirms functional relevance with delivery gaps.
by_protocol.X-MC-L2: X-MC-L2 (Starlight, n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, confidence=developing) shows stable but underwhelming performance. Qualitative (n=20) includes moderate improvement from 6 but some 'no effect'. AutoGluon predicts 7.538, significantly higher than observed, indicating a large real-expected gap. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity. YouTube views (12) are the highest in TRANSFORMING but still minimal.
by_protocol.X-MC-L3: X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing) records the lowest mean in the entire library with the widest variance and a bimodal distribution. Two respondents reported significant improvement, five rated 7–8, but five rated 5 or lower. Qualitative (n=17) shows some improvement but also 'no effect' and one 'worse'. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 — an extreme 1.84-point gap indicating severe underperformance. YouTube views (8) very low. This protocol warrants prototype revision of frequency arc or duration.
by_protocol.X-MD-L1: X-MD-L1 (Footpath, n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful) is one of the weakest TRANSFORMING protocols with mean below 6.4 and only 45% positive — the lowest positive rate in the library. Most report slight or moderate improvement with delayed settling (20 minutes for 5/17 qualitative). AutoGluon predicts 7.876 — the highest predicted score among all protocols — but this protocol underperforms drastically with a 1.52-point gap. Cross-bucket routing confirms intended motivation zone. YouTube views (5) minimal. This is a major model-observation misalignment.
by_protocol.X-MD-L2: X-MD-L2 (Trail, n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing) shows consistently low performance with 43% positive. Some report no effect; settling delayed. AutoGluon predicts 7.876, far above observed, indicating major misalignment. YouTube views (7) minimal. Cross-bucket routing supports mind clarity — possibly indicating functional overlap between motivation and clarity protocols.
by_protocol.X-MD-L3: X-MD-L3 (Switchback, n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing) is a paradoxical result: high mean despite high variance and low n. Qualitative (n=17) reports 'moderate improvement' for some, 'no effect' for others. Settle rapid for 9/13. AutoGluon predicts 7.876, still above observed. YouTube views (7) low. Embedding drift is notable (0.507). This protocol may resonate with a specific subpopulation but the high variance and small n prevent firm conclusions.
by_protocol.X-ME-L1: X-ME-L1 (Breeze, n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful) sits below TRANSFORMING average with moderate variance. Settling times long (20 minutes reported 6/22 qualitative). Music feedback polarized. AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone — significantly above observed — suggesting the protocol may be effective for very low-affect states not yet captured in outcome model. Cross-bucket routing confirms low zone prediction. YouTube views (8) minimal.
by_protocol.X-ME-L2: X-ME-L2 (Sunrise, n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful) shows better performance than L1 with faster settling and more positive music feedback. Qualitative (n=15) shows settle at 10 minutes (7/15) and 5 minutes (4/15), with music 'Liked' (7) and 'Loved' (5). AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone vs observed 6.76 — a persistent gap. YouTube views (8) minimal. This protocol appears more accessible than L1 but still underperforms model expectations.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: X-ME-L3 (Updraft, n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing) is the lowest-scoring Mood & Energy protocol. Qualitative (n=18) shows settle at 5 minutes (8/18), music 'Liked' (5), 'Loved' (4). Change ratings: 'Noticeable' (7), 'Moderate' (5), 'Significant' (4). AutoGluon predicts 8.230 for low zone — a massive gap. YouTube views (6) minimal. Small n and developing confidence limit interpretation but the model-observation divergence is consistent across the X-ME family.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Most listeners with anxiety or stress found Meadow noticeably helpful within about 10 minutes. The music was well-liked, and while experiences varied, the overall response was clearly positive. This is the most tested anxiety protocol so far.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Cottage helps with anxiety but works more gradually — most people settled in about 5 minutes. The music got mixed reviews, some loved it, others found it just okay. It's reliable but less dramatic than Meadow.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Valley takes a bit longer to work (around 10 minutes) and some people didn't feel much effect. The music got neutral reviews. It may be a deeper, slower protocol that needs more patience.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Anchor helps people in acute distress, with many reporting significant improvement within 5–10 minutes. The music is calming and well-liked. Results vary — it seems to work very well for some but less for others.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Harbor also helps in crisis situations but the music got more mixed reactions — some found it neutral. It works similarly to Anchor but feels different sonically.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Horizon works fastest for some people in crisis — several felt better almost immediately. But it's polarizing: some loved it, others really didn't. It may suit certain listeners perfectly and miss others entirely.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Pebble is the most thoroughly tested protocol in the library. Most people with over-stimulation felt noticeable improvement within 5–10 minutes, and the music was widely loved. It's the standout performer.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Rainfall works well for over-stimulation, similar to Pebble but with slightly less dramatic effects. The music got split reviews. It's solid but less striking.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Glacier is consistent and effective for over-stimulation, and notably, several people used it when trying to fall asleep. It works well and may have a secondary benefit for sleep onset.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Lantern is the top sleep protocol — most people settled quickly (within 5 minutes) and really liked the music. It's a strong performer that more people should discover.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Hammock is statistically the most consistent sleep protocol, but the music got neutral reviews, and it's mostly being used by caregivers or clinicians rather than people listening for themselves. That's worth looking into.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Midnight performs reliably for sleep, with quick settling and generally positive feedback. It does what it's designed to do.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Ember helps some people enter creative flow dramatically, while others only notice slight change. The music is liked, but the experience is polarized — it's not consistent across listeners.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Current is the most consistent creative flow protocol — people who respond to it respond well. The music is loved. It works reliably for those it works for.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Aurora shows the strongest results for creative flow so far, with high scores and consistent feedback. It's promising but still early days with fewer total listeners.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Compass is the lowest-scoring focus protocol. Many listeners found the rhythm 'slightly busy' — it may be too rhythmically complex for focus work. This needs adjustment.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Waypoint works well for focus but takes patience — most people settled around 10 minutes. The music is neutral but the results are strong.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Summit is the highest-scoring protocol in the entire library. People loved the music, found the rhythm balanced, and reported significant improvement. It's a standout for focus and clarity.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Stone works for maintenance and balance but takes time — many people needed 20 minutes to settle. The music got neutral reviews. It's effective but slow.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Axis is hit or miss — some people report no effect, others rate it highly. Several found the rhythm too busy for a calming protocol. It's inconsistent and may need rhythm adjustment.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Orbit has a high rate of positive responses for maintenance, though some didn't settle at all. Music reviews are mixed. Promising but early data.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Cavern helps some people with mind clarity but others report delayed settling or even feeling worse. The music is liked but the protocol may not be landing correctly for everyone.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Starlight is stable but underwhelming for mind clarity. Some report moderate improvement, others no effect. It's not hitting its mark consistently yet.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Cosmos is the lowest-scoring protocol in the library. Results are all over the place — some helped, some not, one person felt worse. It needs a redesign.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Footpath is the weakest motivation protocol. Most people report only slight improvement and it takes a long time to settle. The model expects much more — there's a real disconnect.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Trail consistently underperforms for motivation. Low engagement, delayed settling. The model predicts it should work much better — something's misaligned.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Switchback is puzzling — high average score but very mixed individual results and a small sample. It works dramatically for some, not at all for others. Hard to read with this little data.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Breeze hasn't hit its stride for mood and energy yet. Settling takes a long time (20 minutes for several people) and music feedback is split. The model thinks it should work for very low states — but we're not seeing it.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Sunrise is better than Breeze — faster settling, better music feedback — but still well below model predictions. It's more accessible but not there yet.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Updraft is the lowest mood/energy protocol. Quick settling for some, decent music, but the model expects far more. Early data, big gap.
